turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi! How are you doing these days?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A bit tired today, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm reviewing the new spy film for the student paper and I kind of hated it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's okay, honest reviews are more interesting. Would you open with what didn't work, or start with the few things you did like?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hold on, I need to talk to my roommate for a second. Stay quiet until I say I'm back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you check if the baby monitor is on?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The little light's green, so yes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you read this? Is that a teaspoon or a tablespoon of salt?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Your gran's handwriting is something else. Looks like a big T to me.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A big T means tablespoon, right?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Usually. But a tablespoon of salt in one loaf sounds like a lot.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Not that salty. Do half and taste the dough.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: You can't really taste raw dough with yeast in it, can you?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: A tiny pinch won't kill you. Go on.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure thing. So, back to your review. Which end are you starting from?
